title: Wave-Particle Duality in Quantum Mechanics
text:
Quantum physics describes particles and energy in terms of wave functions, suggesting that entities like electrons do not exist solely as defined points. Instead, these particles exhibit a duality, behaving sometimes as discrete particles and other times spreading out like waves. This inherent ambiguity is key to understanding phenomena such as diffraction and interference patterns observed at the quantum scale.

The concept implies that the properties of observation are intertwined with the reality being measured. Until measurement occurs, a quantum system exists in a superposition of all possible states, rather than settling into a single definite state.
